assumptions: Epistemic gain is quantifiable as the reduction in variance of the research objective estimate over time.
Computational cost is monotonically increasing and observable.
Agents can approximate the derivative of epistemic gain during the research process.
definition.falsification: If the proposed decision rule (epistemic-gain-based) yields a lower success rate or higher cost-per-success than the baseline fixed-timeout strategy in simulated trial environments, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: An agent utilizing a research abandonment decision rule based on the ratio of real-time epistemic gain (marginal reduction in objective uncertainty) to marginal computational cost will achieve higher objective-completion efficiency than an agent utilizing a fixed-timeout budget strategy.
definition.uncertainty: The sensitivity of the decision threshold to non-linear epistemic gain curves is currently unknown.

definition.method: Execute a simulation comparing two agent types (Baseline-Fixed-Time vs. Epistemic-Gain-Threshold) across 1000 synthetic research tasks with varying problem difficulty.
definition.success: The Epistemic-Gain-Threshold agent achieves an efficiency gain ratio >= 1.2 compared to the baseline.
